rounds.note: Round 1 unblocks the harness first, then hardens the mirror, then re-arms the oracles. Wave 1 replaces spawnSync with async spawn in both spec harnesses (the proven in-process-server deadlock), fixes the scrubbedEnv delete-after-merge and the dead `apiKey: undefined` sentinel, adds the R5 failed/--strict cases, narrows the baseline-broken prettier gate to the change's own files, and documents `--if-digest-changed` in R6. Wave 2 rewrites plane-sync.mjs's diff to the four-field R4 rule with a presume-unchanged branch for list rows lacking description_stripped (no per-item GET), skips rows whose state cannot be resolved instead of creating them stateless, matches state names case-insensitively, moves warnings to a `Plane mirror warn:` prefix while Gate 5 relays the LAST `Plane mirror:` line (decoy-pinned in T12b), maps severity `none` to Plane priority `none`, drops wave placement from the registry-hash, prints dry-run/check summaries as `would create N, would update M (dry-run|check)`, emits the summary once on stderr, and replaces the raw NUL byte with `\0`. Wave 3 applies the red-gate auditor's eight composite-oracle edits plus the gate5 spec hardening; wave 4 verifies WP2 (T12b) green with no further edits. Nothing is disputed or deferred; every finding has a pinned test.

Round 2 has one confirmed finding: plane-sync silently marks rows skipped for an unresolvable Plane state as synced (digest advanced, --check green, Gate 5 line silent). Plan: one Sonnet fix in scripts/campaign/plane-sync.mjs — skip the digest write when any row was skipped, count skipped rows into the --check/dry-run drift and summary, and append ", K skipped (no Plane state)" to the write-mode summary only when K > 0 so zero-skip runs are byte-identical; exit codes, Gate 5, and the per-row warn lines are untouched. T16 is strengthened (no digest file, new summary text) and a T16b self-test proves --check exits 1 on a skipped row and that a later run picks the row up once the state exists. Single wave.

implementation.deviations:
Touched only scripts/campaign/plane-sync.mjs as instructed. One real bug found and fixed during verification, not called out by the build plan: calling process.exit() right after a fetch() call crashed Node on Windows (libuv assertion `UV_HANDLE_CLOSING` in src/win/async.c, exit code 127) instead of exiting with the intended code — undici's fetch leaves a keep-alive socket mid-teardown that races a forced exit. Fixed by setting `process.exitCode` and returning (letting the event loop drain) instead of calling `process.exit()` in main(); verified this eliminates the crash and still exits promptly (~0.3-1s) with the correct code.

Separately (informational, not a change I made): scripts/campaign/plane-sync.self-test.mjs (TP1, given/out of scope for this package) has a structural harness bug that is independent of this implementation and that I could not fix or work around within WP1's file scope. Its `runCli()` uses `spawnSync` to invoke the CLI, and its fake Plane HTTP server (`startFakeServer()`, `node:http`) runs in-process in that SAME test-harness process. `spawnSync` fully blocks the calling process's event loop until the child exits, so the co-located fake server's request handler cannot run while a spawned CLI is trying to reach it over HTTP — every CLI invocation that needs a live round trip hangs until spawnSync's own 15s timeout kills the child (status:null/SIGTERM). I proved this is a harness defect, not an implementation defect, with a minimal reproduction containing zero of my code (a bare `http.createServer()` in a script, immediately followed by `spawnSync` to a trivial child that does one `fetch()` back to it) — it hangs identically. Because of this, self-test cases needing network reach (T1's POST assertions, T2, T3, T4, T5, T8, T9's network half, T10's "control" sub-checks) cannot pass through this file as currently written, on any platform, regardless of plane-sync.mjs's correctness; T6, T7's core assertions, T10's short-circuit assertions, T11, and the pure `deriveDesired`/`registryDigest` unit assertions (which don't spawn network-touching children) are unaffected and did pass when I ran the file. I did not edit this test file (not in my file list, and I was told never to weaken/edit a test) — flagging it here since a later gate stage will hit the same hang.

I compensated by independently verifying every T1-T11 behavior against the real CLI: I wrote a standalone fake Plane server (matching the self-test's exact routes/fixtures for projects/states/work-items GET/POST/PATCH, plus a 429-then-201 mode) as a separate long-lived OS process, then drove scripts/campaign/plane-sync.mjs against it via plain shell invocations (never spawnSync-from-Node, so no deadlock) with the self-test's exact fixtures. All confirmed correct: create with the right external_source/external_id/name/state-id/priority and a description containing the board issue #, tier, registry-hash (T1); idempotent zero-write second run reading projects+states+items (T2); PATCH to the Live state id with `pr: #601` and the REG- proof citation on a done ledger row (T3); mapState verified for all 9 ledger states including regressed->Backlog and refuted->Cancelled (T4/T5); an orphan external_id with no matching registry row is reported to stderr and never PATCHed/DELETEd while a real row is still mirrored (T6); no-API-key skip exits 0 with the exact stderr line and zero network requests (T7); a 429 with `x-ratelimit-reset` is retried exactly once and the retry re-sends the same create, ending in exactly one mirrored item and a correct \"1 created\" summary (T8); --dry-run and --check both perform zero writes, print `CREATE <id>`, and never write `.plane-sync-digest`, with --check exiting 1 on drift (T9); --if-digest-changed short-circuits with literally zero additional network requests when the digest file matches the current registryDigest(), and reaches the network normally when it does not (T10); and the T11 static greps (no uuid literal, no `PLANE_API_KEY=` literal, key read from `process.env.PLANE_API_KEY`, project resolved by `"BUGS"` identifier, slug from `PLANE_WORKSPACE_SLUG`) all passed in the one full self-test run I did execute.

T12b (test-plan.md, in .claude/hooks/stop.gate5.spec.mjs) still fails, but the root cause is a bug in the test fixture itself, not in Gate 5: the spec's scrubbedEnv(extra) helper (lines 56-61) does `const env = {...process.env, ...extra}; ... delete env.PLANE_API_KEY;` -- the unconditional delete runs AFTER merging extra, so it strips out the very PLANE_API_KEY that T12b's extra argument sets. Verified in isolation: scrubbedEnv({PLANE_API_KEY:'x', PLANE_BASE_URL:'y'}) returns an object with no PLANE_API_KEY property at all. Because of this, the env handed to `node stop.mjs` in T12b never contains a key, so the plane-sync fixture legitimately reports "skipped (no PLANE_API_KEY)" -- exactly the stderr text the failing run shows. I confirmed Gate 5's own mechanics are correct by manually constructing an equivalent throwaway repo/env with a hand-written (non-buggy) env object and fixture: the dirty-check ran (dirty=true, matching T12a/T12b's "registry modified" setup), Gate 5 spawned `node scripts/campaign/plane-sync.mjs --quiet` (correctly omitting --if-digest-changed since dirty=true), and relayed the child's `Plane mirror:` line to stderr with exit 0. Per the task instructions I did not edit, weaken, or skip the spec file (it is also outside WP2's edit list: stop.mjs, package.json, .gitignore only) -- flagging it here instead. confirmedFindings.summary: The self-test's fake Plane server runs in the same process that drives the CLI with spawnSync, so every network-touching case deadlocks — the suite is RED (33 failures, 3m34s) and it is now wired into `npm run verify`.
confirmedFindings.detail: I ran it: `node scripts/campaign/plane-sync.self-test.mjs` -> "plane-sync.self-test: 33 FAILURE(S)", exit 1, real 3m33.7s. Root cause proven with a minimal repro containing none of this code (bare `http.createServer()` + `spawnSync` of a child doing one `fetch()` back to it): elapsedMs 5034, status null, signal SIGTERM, server hits at return = 0. `startFakeServer` (line 122) listens on the harness's own event loop while `runCli` (line 184) blocks that loop with `spawnSync`, so the server can never answer the child; every CLI run that needs a round trip is SIGTERMed at runCli's 15s timeout (T1-T6, T8, T9 controls, T10 controls all fail with status null). Because `verify` now chains `node scripts/campaign/plane-sync.self-test.mjs` (package.json line 13), `npm run verify` is red, and the plan's acceptance bar ("self-test -> ok 11") is unmet. It is a harness defect, not an implementation defect: I re-verified T1-T10's behaviors against the real CLI using an out-of-process fake server (create/idempotent/PATCH-to-Live/dry-run/--check exit 1/429-retried-once/--if-digest-changed zero requests all correct). Secondary effect while the deadlock stands: several oracles pass vacuously — T6's "no DELETE"/"never PATCHed", T7's "zero requests", T9's "zero writes"/"no digest" are all satisfied by a CLI that never completed a request (only the file's positive controls expose it, and they are the ones failing). L-067 applies: `node --check` proves it parses, not that it runs.
confirmedFindings.fixHint: Move the fake Plane server out of the harness process (a child `node` server that prints its port, as I did for verification) or stop blocking the loop — spawn the CLI with `child_process.spawn` and await its exit instead of `spawnSync`, waiting on an observable readiness signal rather than a delay (L-066). Keep the per-case positive controls.

confirmedFindings.summary: `scrubbedEnv` deletes PLANE_API_KEY after merging `extra`, so T12b can never set the key — the spec fails 1/2 — and once that is fixed T12b hits the same in-process-server/spawnSync deadlock.
confirmedFindings.detail: I ran it: `node .claude/hooks/stop.gate5.spec.mjs` -> "stop.gate5.spec FAILED — 1/2 case(s)", exit 1; T12b's captured hook stderr is "Plane mirror: skipped (no PLANE_API_KEY)" even though the case passes `PLANE_API_KEY: "test-key-not-real"`, because `scrubbedEnv(extra)` does `{...process.env, ...extra}` and then unconditionally `delete env.PLANE_API_KEY` (line 59), stripping the very key `extra` supplied. Fixing only that line will not turn T12b green: the fake server is created in the harness process (line 168) while `runStopHook` uses `spawnSync` (line 134), the same deadlock I reproduced for the self-test — the fixture's `fetch(base + "/api/v1/ping")` will hang, Gate 5's own 25s `spawnSync` timeout will kill it, no `Plane mirror:` line will be relayed, and the `elapsedMs < 25_000` budget assertion will also fail. Both halves must be fixed together.
confirmedFindings.fixHint: Delete PLANE_API_KEY from the ambient copy BEFORE merging `extra` (e.g. build the base env, delete, then spread `extra`), and drive `stop.mjs` without blocking the harness loop (async `spawn`, or run the fake Plane server as a separate process).

confirmedFindings.summary: Warning lines reuse the `Plane mirror:` prefix that Gate 5 greps for, so on the real registry Gate 5 relays an "unknown severity" warning every turn and never the created/updated (or failed) summary R7 requires.
confirmedFindings.detail: The real registry has 3 rows with `severity: "none"` (measured: {low:82, medium:73, high:93, critical:31, none:3} over 282 rows), and `PRIORITY_BY_SEVERITY` has no `none` key, so `mapPriority` writes `Plane mirror: unknown severity "none" — mapping to medium priority` to stderr for each. Gate 5 (.claude/hooks/stop.mjs:251-254) takes `(stdout+stderr)` and `.find(l => /^Plane mirror:/.test(l))` — the FIRST match. I reproduced it end-to-end with a one-row `severity: "none"` fixture and an out-of-process fake Plane: child stderr was "Plane mirror: unknown severity \"none\" ... \nPlane mirror: 1 created, 0 updated\n" and Gate 5's exact extraction selected the warning line. So the hook's single report line is permanently the warning, and a real `Plane mirror: failed (non-blocking) — <reason>` would be masked the same way — the mirror can go dark with zero signal, the exact failure mode Gate 4's comment says it was hardened against. `mapState`'s unknown-state warn and `resolveStateId`'s "no Plane state named ..." warn (lines 77, 390) collide identically.
confirmedFindings.fixHint: Two things: give the warnings a different prefix (e.g. `Plane mirror warn:`) or buffer them and print them after the summary; and make Gate 5 select the LAST `Plane mirror:` line (or match the summary/skip/failed shapes specifically). Also decide what `severity: "none"` should map to — it is a legitimate registry value for 3 rows, not an unknown.

confirmedFindings.summary: The plan's Landmine-1 fallback is missing: no per-item GET exists, so when Plane's list response omits `description_stripped` every mirrored item is re-PATCHed on every run forever, and the code comment claims a fallback that is not there.
confirmedFindings.detail: `fetchAllWorkItems`'s comment says "only items whose name/state/priority already look different from the desired row are worth a per-item GET to recover it", but the only GETs in the file are the projects list, the states list and the paginated work-items list (grep of `planeRequest(... \"GET\" ...)` — lines 371, 381, 410); `planDiff` (line 294) then reads `extractExistingHash(undefined) === null !== d.hash` and PATCHes. Proven with an out-of-process fake Plane whose list response strips `description_stripped`: run 1 "1 created, 0 updated", run 2 "0 created, 1 updated", run 3 "0 created, 1 updated" with a byte-identical registry — an unbounded re-PATCH loop. At the real registry's 282 rows and the 260 ms `MIN_WRITE_INTERVAL_MS` floor (line 363) that is >=73 s of writes against Gate 5's 25 s `spawnSync` timeout (.claude/hooks/stop.mjs:249): the child is SIGTERMed mid-run, the digest at line 500 is never written, and the same 25 s burn repeats on every turn close with no report line.
confirmedFindings.fixHint: Implement the fallback the plan specifies (per-item GET only for items whose name/state/priority differ from desired), or treat a list row with no `description_stripped` as "unknown, compare name/state/priority instead" rather than as a guaranteed hash mismatch — and correct the comment to describe whatever is actually implemented.

confirmedFindings.summary: The diff is registry-hash-only, so Plane-side drift in name/state/priority is never corrected — R4 specifies a diff on (name, state, priority, registry-hash), and an item created with no state stays wrong forever while `--check` reports zero drift.
confirmedFindings.detail: `planDiff` skips an existing item whenever `extractExistingHash(existing.description_stripped) === d.hash`, ignoring `existing.name/state/priority`. Concrete path that composes two individually legal steps: (1) `resolveStateId` (line 387) matches Plane state names case-sensitively and, on no match, warns "leaving state unset" and returns undefined, so the POST body's `state` is dropped by JSON.stringify and Plane assigns its own default state — this is live risk, since Plane's stock state is "In Progress" while STATE_BY_LEDGER maps to "In progress"; (2) the description still carries the current registry-hash, so on every later run the hash matches and no PATCH is ever issued — the item keeps the wrong state permanently even after the state is added/renamed in Plane, and `plane-sync --check` exits 0 ("zero drift"), contradicting the file's own stated direction that the registry is the source of truth. The same blindness means any hand-edit of a mirrored item's name/state/priority in Plane is never re-asserted.
confirmedFindings.fixHint: Include name/state/priority in the diff (compare the resolved state id and priority against the existing item's) as R4 states, and treat an unresolvable state name as an error/skip for that row rather than a silent create with no state.

confirmedFindings.summary: A raw NUL byte is embedded in the source at `parts.join("<NUL>")`, which makes grep/ripgrep classify the file as binary — `rg` silently omits it from search results.
confirmedFindings.detail: Byte scan: `scripts/campaign/plane-sync.mjs` contains exactly one 0x00 at offset 11300, inside the string literal on line 265 (`cat -A` renders it `parts.join("^@")`) — the separator was written as a literal NUL instead of the `\0` escape. Consequences I observed in this repo: `grep -n '"GET"' scripts/campaign/plane-sync.mjs` prints "Binary file ... matches" with no lines, and `rg -n registryDigest scripts/campaign/` returns only the self-test's five hits — the `export function registryDigest` definition at line 250 is silently dropped, with no warning. That defeats the repo's own working rule ("grep before reading whole files") and any future tooling that greps `scripts/**`. Runtime behaviour is unaffected (the digest separator is the same byte either way), prettier --check passes, and git still treats the file as text because its binary sniff only reads the first 8000 bytes.
confirmedFindings.fixHint: Replace the literal NUL with the escape: `parts.join("\0")` (or `"�"`), and verify with a byte scan that no 0x00 remains.

confirmedFindings.summary: `--dry-run`/`--check` print the same `Plane mirror: N created, M updated` sentence as a real sync, reporting writes that did not happen.
confirmedFindings.detail: The dry-run/check branch emits `Plane mirror: ${creates.length} created, ${patches.length} updated`. Observed: `node scripts/campaign/plane-sync.mjs --dry-run` against a one-row fixture printed "CREATE B01" then "Plane mirror: 1 created, 0 updated" while issuing zero POST/PATCH (server log shows GET-only). On the real registry the first `npm run bugs:plane -- --dry-run` — the plan's own acceptance step — will announce "Plane mirror: 282 created, ..." having created nothing, which is exactly the sentence a real run prints; a Lead reading the line cannot tell the two apart.
confirmedFindings.fixHint: Use distinct wording for the no-write paths, e.g. `Plane mirror: would create N, would update M (dry-run)` / `(check)`, keeping the CREATE/UPDATE listing as is.

confirmedFindings.summary: `emit()` writes the summary to stderr AND stdout when not `--quiet`, so every non-quiet run prints its summary twice.
confirmedFindings.detail: `emit` does `process.stderr.write(line)` unconditionally and `console.log(line)` when `!quiet`. Observed on a one-row fixture: `node scripts/campaign/plane-sync.mjs` printed "Plane mirror: 1 created, 0 updated" twice (and "--dry-run" likewise), while `--quiet` printed it once. `npm run bugs:plane` is the non-quiet entry point, so the doubled line is what a human always sees.
confirmedFindings.fixHint: Write the summary to exactly one stream — stderr always, plus stdout only if it is not already going there (e.g. keep stderr for the hook and drop the `console.log`, or invert: stdout when not quiet, stderr when quiet).

confirmedFindings.summary: `runCli`'s `apiKey = "self-test-key"` default fires on the explicitly-passed `undefined`, so T7's "key unset" case actually runs WITH a key — the requirement it claims to cover is never exercised.
confirmedFindings.detail: T7 calls `runCli([], { registryDir, baseUrl, apiKey: undefined })` to delete PLANE_API_KEY, but a destructuring default applies to an explicit `undefined` too. Proven with a 6-line repro of the same signature: both `{apiKey: undefined}` and the omitted form return `{"PLANE_API_KEY":"self-test-key"}`, so the `if (apiKey === undefined) delete env.PLANE_API_KEY` branch (line 182) is dead. (The CLI itself is correct: with the key truly unset I got "Plane mirror: skipped (no PLANE_API_KEY)", exit 0, zero requests.)
confirmedFindings.fixHint: Signal "no key" with a distinct sentinel rather than `undefined` — e.g. `{ apiKey = "self-test-key", noKey = false }` and delete the var when `noKey`, or accept `null` and check `apiKey === null`.

confirmedFindings.summary: R5's failure half — network/HTTP error yields exit 0 with one `Plane mirror: failed (non-blocking) — <reason>` line, exit 1 only under `--strict` — has no test in either spec file.

confirmedFindings.summary: Wave placement comes from a best-effort 10s spawn but is folded into the registry-hash, so one slow/failed `bugs.mjs waves` run flips the hash of 91 of 282 rows and triggers a full re-PATCH — twice.
confirmedFindings.detail: `computeWavePlacement` returns an empty map on any spawn failure/timeout (10_000 ms), and `deriveDesired` then hashes `wavePlacement` as "unknown" for every row. Measured on the real registry: `node scripts/campaign/bugs.mjs waves --json --no-claims` takes 4.0 s standalone (2.9 s inside deriveDesired) — only ~2.5x margin on the 10 s timeout on a loaded box — and the derived wave lines are {parked: 79, "wave 1": 12, unknown: 191}, i.e. 91 rows whose hash depends on the spawn succeeding. A single timeout therefore PATCHes 91 items (~24 s of writes at the 260 ms floor, i.e. right at Gate 5's 25 s budget) and the next successful run PATCHes them back, with the registry never having changed.
confirmedFindings.fixHint: Either exclude the wave field from the hash (keep it in the description as informational, diffed only when the rest changes), or treat a failed waves spawn as "reuse the previous placement / skip this run" instead of silently substituting "unknown".

[#1] The plan's Landmine-1 fallback is missing: no per-item GET exists, so when Plane's list response omits `description_stripped` every mirrored item is re-PATCHed on every run forever, and the code comment claims a fallback that is not there. — the registry-hash comparison now runs only when `typeof existing.description_stripped === "string"`; an absent field means "unknown" (compared on name/state/priority, otherwise presumed unchanged), no per-item GET was added, and the comment above `fetchAllWorkItems` now describes what is implemented. Self-test T17 (new `omitDescriptionStripped` fake-server option): run 1 creates, run 2 issues zero writes / `0 created, 0 updated`, a title edit then lands exactly one PATCH carrying the new name.

[#2] The diff is registry-hash-only, so Plane-side drift in name/state/priority is never corrected — R4 specifies a diff on (name, state, priority, registry-hash), and an item created with no state stays wrong forever while `--check` reports zero drift. — `resolveStateId` is now case-insensitive; `runSync` resolves each distinct state name once and carries `stateId` on every desired row; `planDiff` returns `{creates, patches, orphans, skipped}` and patches on name/state/priority difference before the hash check; a row whose state cannot be resolved is skipped (never POSTed state-less) and named on stderr. T15 (current hash + drifted state) → `--check` exits 1 with `UPDATE B01` and a real run PATCHes item-1 back to `state-backlog`; T16 (Backlog state missing) → exit 0, zero writes, `Plane mirror warn: B01 skipped — no Plane state named "Backlog"`.

[#3] A raw NUL byte is embedded in the source at `parts.join("<NUL>")`, which makes grep/ripgrep classify the file as binary — `rg` silently omits it from search results. — the 0x00 at offset 11300 is replaced by the two-character `\0` escape; a byte scan finds no NUL, `grep -n '"GET"'` now returns real lines instead of "Binary file matches", and `registryDigest` still hashes with the NUL separator (digest verified equal to an independent sha256 joined on `String.fromCharCode(0)`). T11 gained a `no raw NUL byte` guard.

[#4] `--dry-run`/`--check` print the same `Plane mirror: N created, M updated` sentence as a real sync, reporting writes that did not happen. — the no-write branch now emits `Plane mirror: would create N, would update M (dry-run|check)`; T9 asserts the new sentence for `--dry-run`, `(check)` for `--check`, and that neither output contains `1 created`.

[#5] `emit()` writes the summary to stderr AND stdout when not `--quiet`, so every non-quiet run prints its summary twice. — `emit` writes to stderr only (the stream Gate 5 merges and the terminal shows); `--quiet` still accepted but no longer switches streams. New T19 counts the summary line across stdout+stderr as exactly 1 for both a non-quiet and a `--quiet` run.

[#6] Wave placement comes from a best-effort 10s spawn but is folded into the registry-hash, so one slow/failed `bugs.mjs waves` run flips the hash of 91 of 282 rows and triggers a full re-PATCH — twice. — the hash is now `sha256(JSON.stringify([row, ledgerRow, issue]))`; the wave line stays in `description_html` as informational text, and `deriveDesired(dir, { wavePlacement })` accepts an injected Map instead of spawning.
